chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds, so We shall render them as scattered floating dust.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! Even if their deeds were more intensely whiter than the Coptic tapestry, but whenever the Prohibition was presented to them, they were not leaving it.'

key_terms.الْقَبَاطِيِّ: Coptic tapestry / Fine linen (used as a metaphor for extreme whiteness/purity)
key_terms.قَدِمْنا: We will proceed to / We will count
key_terms.هَباءً مَنْثُوراً: Scattered floating dust / Fine dust blown about

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah say He will render the deeds of disbelievers as scattered dust according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates Surah Al-Furqan verse 23 by using the metaphor of 'whiteness' to signify that the deeds of the hypocrites were abundant and pure in appearance, yet rendered void by a single critical flaw: the failure to abstain from the forbidden when it arose. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the necessity of consistent adherence to prohibitions, where even minor neglect of haram can nullify extensive righteous acts, underscoring the fragility of faith without vigilance against sin.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [25:23] And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds, so We shall render them as scattered floating dust. Heasws said: ‘But, by Allahazwj! Even if their deeds were more intensely whiter than the Coptic tapestry, but whenever the Prohibition was presented to them, they were not leaving it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “

I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘We shall call their deeds into Our presence and scatter them into the air as dust (turn them devoid of all virtue).’ [25:23] The Imam said, ‘I swear by Allah, even though their deeds may have been whiter than the Coptic gown, the nullification of such deed is because on their encountering an unlawful matter they did not stay away from it.’”
